# OpenCode SuperNudge A plugin for when you really want to make sure your agents never forget about super important things. ## Use cases Here are examples of `nudges` I use in my workflows which improve agent code-quality ; because I remind them of this ALL the time. ```jsonc { "prompts": [ "~/.config/opencode/snippet/tdd.md", "~/.config/opencode/snippet/no-mocking.md", "~/.config/opencode/snippet/givenwhenthen.md", "~/.config/opencode/snippet/test-pollution.md", "~/.config/opencode/snippet/docstring-pollution.md", "~/.config/opencode/snippet/disable-question-tool.md" ] } ``` ### Forcing TDD (red-green) development ```md TDD: YOU MUST respect the RED / GREEN principle - you ALWAYS write a FAILING test case FIRST - this will ENSURE your changes actually fix the problem. ``` ### Forcing e2e tests without mocking ```md Do NOT use MOCKING, EXCEPT when calling external vendors incurs a real life $$$ COST; otherwise we must stick with REAL e2e test cases at the outer-most user-facing SEAM. ``` ### Forcing the GivenWhenThen forms for test cases ```md You MUST define acceptance criteria in the GivenWhenThen form UNLESS the current project's style guidelines DICTATE otherwise. ``` ### Hedging against too many useless test case creations ```md Be very wary of creating too many test cases. Test the inputs and the outputs of what the user will do at the seams of the application. No more, no less. We don't want to test cases that are extreme outliers. ``` ### Hedging against docstring and comment pollution ```md Do NOT add test docstrings, or comments, or module docstrings unless ABSOLUTELY necessary. ``` ### Soft-disabling the often-slow 'question' tool ```md Do NOT use the question tool at you disposal, it is extremely slow. ``` ## Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/kevincojean/opencode-supernudge.git cd opencode-supernudge npm install ``` Add to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` `plugin` array, replacing `` with the absolute path to your clone: ```jsonc "plugin": [ "" ] ``` ## Config Create `~/.config/opencode/opencode-supernudge/supernudge-configuration.jsonc`: ```jsonc { "prompts": ["~/prompts/style.md", "~/prompts/constraints.md"], "injection.interval": 1, "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": true, "injection.resetCounterOnCompaction": true, "injection.subagentInterval": 1, "injection.subagentAlwaysOnFirst": true, "injection.subagentResetOnCompaction": true, "position.normalMessage": "start", "position.subagent": "start", "position.compaction": "start", "enabled.normalMessage": true, "enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge": true, "enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge": true, "enabled.compaction": true, "wrapper.prefix": "", "wrapper.suffix": "", "nudge.visible": true, "nudge.visibleMarker": true } ``` ### Prompt path resolution
Project-local config A project-local config file can overlay the global config. Two global config keys control this: | Key | Type | Default | Description | |-----|------|---------|-------------| | `currentWorkingDirectory.configFilePath` | string | `"./.opencode/com.kevincojean.opencode-supernudge/supernudge-configuration.jsonc"` | Path to local config (relative to opencode cwd) | | `currentWorkingDirectory.configEnabled` | boolean | `true` | Master switch for local config lookup | When enabled, the plugin looks for a local config file. If found and valid, the local config's `prompts` array is **merged** with the global config's `prompts` array. #### Locally overridable keys | Key | Locally overridable? | |-----|---------------------| | `prompts` | **YES** (concatenated with global) | **Keys overridable within `prompt` objects: | Prompt-key | Overridable? | |-----|---------------------| | `injection.interval` | YES | | `injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage` | YES | | `injection.resetCounterOnCompaction` | NO | | `position.normalMessage` | YES | | `position.subagent` | YES | | `position.compaction` | YES | | `enabled.normalMessage` | YES | | `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge` | YES | | `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` | YES | | `enabled.compaction` | YES | | `wrapper.prefix` | NO | | `wrapper.suffix` | NO | | `nudge.separator` | NO | | `nudge.enableTitlePrefix` | NO | | `nudge.trim` | NO | | `nudge.visible` | YES | | `nudge.visibleMarker` | YES | | `injection.skipFirstMessageBelowChars` | NO | | `injection.subagentInterval` | YES | | `injection.subagentAlwaysOnFirst` | YES | | `injection.subagentResetOnCompaction` | NO | | `currentWorkingDirectory.configFilePath` | NO | | `currentWorkingDirectory.configEnabled` | NO | Example local config: ```jsonc { "prompts": [ ".opencode/com.kevincojean.opencode-supernudge/project-specific-nudge.md", { "path": ".opencode/com.kevincojean.opencode-supernudge/project-specific-nudge.md/tdd.md", "injection.interval": 3, "enabled.compaction": false } ] } ```
Prompt file paths in the `prompts` array support 3 modes: 1. **Home directory** - paths starting with `~` or containing `$HOME`: ```jsonc { "prompts": ["~/prompts/tdd.md", "$HOME/prompts/no-mocking.md"] } ``` 2. **Relative paths** - resolved against opencode's __working directory__: ```jsonc { "prompts": ["./prompts/tdd.md", "prompts/no-mocking.md", "../shared/constraints.md"] } ``` 3. **Absolute paths** - paths starting with `/` are used as-is: ```jsonc { "prompts": ["/home/user/prompts/tdd.md"] } ```
Subagent nudge paths There are **two distinct paths** for injecting nudges into subagent contexts. They are gated separately and have independent defaults: - **System prompt nudge** (`enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge`, default `true`): injects the nudge into the subagent's **initial system prompt** via `experimental.chat.system.transform`. Fires **once** per subagent session, before the subagent starts working. This is the path that gives the subagent the nudge "at the system prompt level" you observe. - **Autonomous work nudge** (`enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge`, default `true`): injects the nudge **periodically** during subagent autonomous turns (via `experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform`). Does NOT fire on the primary agent's `chat.message` - the primary path uses `enabled.normalMessage` instead. To disable periodic nudges, set: ```jsonc { "enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge": false } ``` > The legacy key `enabled.subagent` is no longer recognized. If your config still has it, replace it with the two `enabled.subagent*` keys above.
Per-prompt override ### Per-prompt override Any prompt entry can be an object that overrides specific global settings for that prompt only. String entries use all global defaults. ```jsonc { "prompts": [ // String: global defaults apply "~/prompts/tdd.md", // Object with partial overrides: only listed keys override globals { "path": "~/prompts/givenwhenthen.md", "injection.interval": 3, "injection.skipFirstMessageBelowChars": 10 }, // Object with all overrides: every global setting overridden { "path": "~/prompts/no-mocking.md", "enabled.compaction": false, "enabled.normalMessage": true, "enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge": false, "enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge": false, "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": false, "injection.interval": 1, "injection.resetCounterOnCompaction": false, "injection.skipFirstMessageBelowChars": 10, "injection.subagentInterval": 1, "injection.subagentAlwaysOnFirst": false, "injection.subagentResetOnCompaction": false, "position.compaction": "end", "position.normalMessage": "end", "position.subagent": "end" } ], "injection.interval": 1, "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": true } ``` - `tdd.md` - string, all global defaults - `givenwhenthen.md` - partial override, injects every 3rd message only - `no-mocking.md` - full override, all globals ignored, uses its own settings exclusively
Skipping injections in system contexts ### Skipping injections in system contexts You may chose for nudges to not fire using regexes. For instance, the oh-my-openagent plugin injects prompts when sub-agents finish a task, and it's wasteful to inject in those messages. Use `injection.skipOnRegexMatch` to suppress nudges when text contains markers: ```jsonc { "injection.skipOnRegexMatch": [ "<\\/?system-reminder>" ] } ```
Hidden nudges ### Hidden nudges By default the nudge block is prepended/appended into your message text, so it shows up in the chat. Set `nudge.visible` to `false` to keep your message untouched and deliver the nudge as a separate hidden `synthetic` text part instead. The model still sees it; the chat UI does not render it, and it is never written to the session store. Set `nudge.visibleMarker` to `false` to suppress the `wrapper.prefix`/`wrapper.suffix` marker around each nudge block, even when those strings are non-empty. The nudge text is still injected, just without the wrapper. Both keys are overridable per-prompt. Both are no-ops for the system-prompt and compaction paths, where you never see the content anyway. ```jsonc { "nudge.visible": false, "nudge.visibleMarker": false } ```
### Parameters | Key | Type | Default | Description | |-----|------|---------|-------------| | `prompts` | `(string \| object)[]` | `[]` | Prompt file paths. String or `{ path: string, ...overrides }`. Supports `~`, `$HOME` interpolation, and relative paths (resolved against opencode's working directory). | | `injection.interval` | `number` | `1` | Inject every Nth *user* message. `1` = every message. `2` = 1st, skip 2nd, inject 3rd. | | `injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage` | `boolean` | `true` | Force inject on first user message regardless of interval. | | `injection.resetCounterOnCompaction` | `boolean` | `true` | Reset per-session counter to 0 when compaction fires. | | `position.normalMessage` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"start"` | Nudge placement in user message. `start` = before user text. `end` = after. | | `position.subagent` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"start"` | Nudge placement in subagent workflows.| | `position.compaction` | `"start"` \| `"end"` | `"start"` | Nudge placement in compaction context. | | `enabled.normalMessage` | `boolean` | `true` | Inject nudge on user messages. | | `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge` | `boolean` | `true` | Inject nudge into subagent's **initial system prompt** (via `experimental.chat.system.transform`). Fires once per subagent session. | | `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` | `boolean` | `true` | Inject nudge **periodically** during subagent autonomous turns (via `experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform`). Does NOT fire on the primary agent's `chat.message`. | | `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` | `boolean` | `true` | Inject nudge **periodically** during subagent autonomous turns (via `experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform`). Does NOT fire on the primary agent's `chat.message`. | | `enabled.compaction` | `boolean` | `true` | Inject nudge into context on compaction. | | `wrapper.prefix` | `string` | `""` | Marker inserted above each nudge block. Empty string disables. | | `wrapper.suffix` | `string` | `""` | Marker inserted below each nudge block. Empty string disables. | | `nudge.separator` | `string` | `"\n\n"` | Separator between multiple nudges within the same block. | | `nudge.enableTitlePrefix` | `boolean` | `true` | Prefix each nudge with `[filename]` (lowercase, no extension). | | `nudge.visible` | `boolean` | `true` | Deliver the nudge inside the user's message (visible in chat). When `false`, the user message is left untouched and the nudge is delivered as a hidden `synthetic` text part that only the model sees. | | `nudge.visibleMarker` | `boolean` | `true` | Emit `wrapper.prefix`/`wrapper.suffix` around each nudge block. When `false`, the wrapper is suppressed even if the strings are non-empty. | | `injection.skipFirstMessageBelowChars` | `number` | `3` | Skip injection when user message length `<=` this threshold. | | `injection.skipOnRegexMatch` | `string[]` | `[]` | Skip injection if message text matches any regex. | | `injection.subagentInterval` | `number` | `1` | Inject every Nth autonomous turn. `1` = every turn. `2` = 1st, skip 2nd, inject 3rd. | | `injection.subagentAlwaysOnFirst` | `boolean` | `true` | Force inject on first autonomous turn regardless of interval. | | `injection.subagentResetOnCompaction` | `boolean` | `true` | Reset autonomous counter to 0 when compaction fires. | All parameters except `prompts` can be overridden per-prompt by including them in the prompt object.
Test ```bash # Unit tests node --import tsx --test src/test/supernudge.test.ts # E2E tests (spins up opencode serve with an internal stub LLM server) # SN_E2E_NO_BWRAP=1 is set by default in package.json to avoid bwrap process kill issues # Remove it from package.json to use bwrap sandboxing instead npm run test:e2e ```

# Architecture / Design Decisions

## 2026-08-26

### T-001: Two-flag split for subagent context nudges
T-001 (periodic autonomous nudge) initially proposed `enabled.autonomous` as a new master switch separate from `enabled.subagent`. Review surfaced that this collided semantically: `enabled.subagent` already gates the existing `experimental.chat.system.transform` injection (first-turn nudge into subagent's system prompt). Reviewer resolved: keep the existing behavior intact under `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge` (default `true`), add a NEW master switch `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` (default `false`) for the periodic behavior. No compat shim - `enabled.subagent` removed entirely. The single `SubAgentMessageInjector` class handles both primary-agent (`chat.message`) and subagent (`experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform`) periodic paths, gated by `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge`.

### T-001: Position reuse for autonomous placement
The initial design added `position.autonomous` as a new key. Reviewer collapsed it onto the existing `position.subagent` - one position controls all subagent-context nudges (system.transform first turn + autonomous per turn). Reduces key count by 1 without losing expressiveness.

### Outside-in TDD: chat.message early-return trap
Step 2 (GREEN) hit a structural trap: the existing chat.message handler early-returns when both `startTexts` and `endTexts` are empty (i.e. no user-message injection). With `enabled.normalMessage=false` and only the autonomous path active, the early-return prevented the autonomous code from running. Fix: replace the early-return with a `let target = ...` + `if (!target) return` guard that always locates the target text part before any injection logic runs. Both user-message and autonomous paths then share the same target and mutate it independently.

### `incrementTurnCount` semantics: pre-increment + read
Design choice for `SubAgentMessageInjector`: `incrementTurnCount(sessionID, promptIndex)` is called BEFORE `inject(...)`. `inject` reads the post-increment value from internal state and decides whether to fire. This keeps the increment and the gating as separate atomic calls the plugin entry can order, and avoids passing the count value around.

### V1 vs V2 SDK `EventSessionDeleted` shape mismatch
The `@opencode-ai/plugin` package re-exports `Event` from `@opencode-ai/sdk` (V1). V1's `EventSessionDeleted.properties` only has `info: Session` (no top-level `sessionID`). V2 SDK adds `properties.sessionID: string`. To extract sessionID at the plugin seam, use `event.properties.info.id`. The plugin handles both shapes defensively (V1 path AND V2 sync variant `sync` + `session.deleted.1` + `data.sessionID`). Initial design assumed V2 - corrected when typecheck flagged the missing property on V1.

### Hook spread order matters when composing injector hooks
When `SubAgentMessageInjector.hooks()` returns `Partial<Hooks>`, spreading it into the returned `Hooks` object overwrites any same-named hook from the existing plugin entry. For step 7-10 the injector defined `experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform` (new keys, no collision). For step 11+ it must NOT define `experimental.session.compacting` because that handler already exists in the entry - the entry calls `subAgentInjector.resetOnCompaction(...)` directly. Same for `event` (step 13+14): injector defines it because nothing else does. Lesson: only put new hooks in `hooks()`. Modify existing hook behavior via dedicated methods called from the existing handler.

### `loadPlugin()` return-type typing: prefer `typeof mod.default`
The test helper's typed signature was `{ "chat.message"?: ...; "experimental.chat.system.transform"?: ...; "experimental.session.compacting"?: ... }`. As new hooks were added (text.complete, messages.transform, event), the type had to widen. Cleanest replacement: `Promise<typeof import("../main/index.ts")["default"]>` - lets the test directly reflect whatever the plugin entry returns, no manual type upkeep. Side effect: tests use `const hooks = await plugin(...)` then `hooks["new.hook"]!` - the type narrows correctly because `Hooks` is the actual returned type from the plugin.

### Step 3 (per-prompt isolation) passed without RED-first
The per-prompt counter array design inherently isolates counters - the test for two prompts with different intervals passed on first run. No additional fix needed. Same for step 5 (counter independence) - test passed immediately. This is the correct TDD outcome when the design is right: AC is satisfied and the test confirms it without revealing implementation gaps.

### E2E AC10: subagent multi-turn verification deferred - test env limitation
First AC10 attempt used `agent: "quick"` subagent prompt via `session.prompt`. Diagnostic showed `messages=0` - the subagent never actually ran. Root cause: the e2e stub LLM server returns a canned "stub response" with no tool use, and `agent: "quick"` likely doesn't exist or doesn't execute in the test opencode runtime. Existing AC3 (which uses the same setup) passes vacuously because it only asserts `messages.data !== undefined` - true even for empty array. The e2e suite has a pre-existing gap: no test actually verifies a subagent executes.

Fix path: rewrote AC10 to verify PRIMARY-agent periodic nudge via `sendMessages(["hello-one", "hello-two", "hello-three"])` in same session with `injection.subagentInterval=2`. Mirrors the unit test at step 1 (which already passes). The primary-agent path uses `chat.message` which fires per prompt and calls `subAgentInjector.incrementTurnCount` + `inject`. This validates the wiring through real opencode runtime, just for primary context.

Subagent-context autonomous nudge e2e validation deferred until either (a) a working stub LLM drives multi-turn subagent output, or (b) a real LLM is wired in ($$$ cost). Unit tests at step 7-10 still validate the hook wiring at the seam for subagent path.

### E2E `writeNudgeConfig` whitelist dropped new config keys
Second AC10 attempt failed with 1st message missing NUDGE. Root cause: `writeNudgeConfig` in `e2e.test.ts` builds a `full` object with an explicit whitelist of known keys and drops anything not in the list. The new autonomous keys (`enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge`, `injection.subagentInterval`, etc.) were silently omitted from the written config file, so the plugin used defaults (`false` = autonomous path disabled). Fix: add all 4 new keys to the whitelist with defaults matching plugin DEFAULTS. Lesson: when adding new config keys, the e2e `writeNudgeConfig` whitelist must be updated in the same change - it's a second source of truth for config shape.

### AC10 final shape: primary-agent periodic verification
AC10 now verifies primary-agent periodic nudge: `enabled.normalMessage=false`, `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge=false`, `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=true`, `injection.subagentInterval=2`, `injection.subagentAlwaysOnFirst=true`. Sends 3 messages in same session via `sendMessages(["hello-one","hello-two","hello-three"])`. Asserts 1st + 3rd contain NUDGE, 2nd does not. This mirrors the unit test at step 1 and validates the wiring through real opencode runtime. PASSES.

### T-001 default flip: autonomous nudge ON by default
User-requested reversal of the original T-001 reviewer's choice. Changed DEFAULTS:
- `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge`: `false` -> `true`
- `injection.subagentResetOnCompaction`: `false` -> `true`

Rationale: user wants periodic nudges active out-of-the-box for this plugin's purpose. Old `false` defaults were conservative opt-ins; new `true` defaults make the autonomous path fire without config.

### T-001 default flip: side-effect on primary chat.message
Flipping `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=true` activates BOTH paths the gate controls: primary-agent `chat.message` and subagent `experimental.text.complete` + `experimental.chat.messages.transform`. With default `enabled.normalMessage=true` also true, every primary user message now fires BOTH the normal-message nudge and the autonomous nudge in sequence - producing two nudge blocks per turn. The 23 existing unit tests assumed single-injection and broke. Mitigation: modified `writeConfigFile` test helper with third arg `injectConservativeDefaults` (default `true`) that injects `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=false` and `injection.subagentResetOnCompaction=false` unless overridden. Failing tests preserved original intent automatically; two new RED-tests verifying actual plugin defaults opt out via the third arg. Real-world users see double injection on primary chat unless they set `enabled.normalMessage=false` or `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=false`. Noted in README.

### Helper-divergence principle for test config writers
When flipping a DEFAULTS value, prefer modifying the test-config helper to inject the OLD default conservatively (preserving existing test isolation) over mass-updating every test that uses the helper. New tests that exercise actual plugin defaults opt out via a flag. Trade-off: tests diverge from production defaults - helper is a test convenience, production code is unaffected. Lesson: a test config helper is a second source of truth for behavior, treat its default injection policy as a deliberate choice.

### T-001 bug fix: remove autonomous path from chat.message
After flipping `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` default to true (T-001 default-flip entry), primary agent's `chat.message` fired BOTH `enabled.normalMessage` and the `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` paths, producing two nudge blocks per user turn (one wrapped normalMessage + one raw autonomous). User observation: primary agents had double injection, subagents did not. Root cause: the original T-001 architecture decision gated BOTH primary chat.message and subagent experimental hooks behind the same `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` flag, but that conflates two distinct semantics: primary chat.message already has `enabled.normalMessage` for user-message nudging. Fix: removed the autonomous inject loop from `chat.message` handler entirely. Autonomous counter is now only incremented via `experimental.text.complete` (shared by both primary and subagent text completions), and autonomous injection only fires via `experimental.chat.messages.transform`. Result: primary chat.message fires ONLY normalMessage (1 nudge per turn by default); subagent experimental hooks fire autonomous (1 nudge per autonomous turn by default). Deleted 3 tests that asserted chat.message's autonomous path (dead code after fix): "chat.message 3 turns with subagentInterval=2", "two prompts independent counters via chat.message", "normalMessage+autonomous on same chat.message". New test added: "chat.message with default config fires exactly ONE nudge block". RED->GREEN verified at the seam.

### T-001 bug fix part 2: gate messages.transform for primary sessions
Removing the chat.message autonomous path was not enough - user reported still seeing double injection on primary agents. Root cause: `experimental.chat.messages.transform` fires for BOTH primary chat.message flow and subagent LLM calls, and it was injecting autonomous on both. For primary chat.message flow, chat.message's normalMessage inject runs first, then messages.transform injects autonomous on top -> 2 nudges per primary turn. Fix: track which sessions are "primary" vs "subagent" via the `event` hook listening to `session.created` / `session.updated` events. The opencode SDK's `Session` type has `parentID?: string` - present for subagent sessions, absent for primary. Added `primarySessions: Set<string>` to `SubAgentMessageInjector`. On session.created/updated, add to set if no parentID (primary) or remove from set if parentID present (subagent). On session.deleted, remove from set. `experimental.chat.messages.transform` now returns early if `sessionID` is in `primarySessions`. Result: primary chat.message flow gets ONLY normalMessage (1 nudge per turn); subagent LLM calls get autonomous via messages.transform (1 nudge per autonomous turn). Default behavior preserved when session.created event hasn't fired yet (set is empty, default to inject). New tests: "primary session.created without parentID -> messages.transform does NOT inject", "subagent session.created with parentID -> messages.transform DOES inject". RED->GREEN verified at the seam. 50/50 unit tests pass, typecheck clean. E2E deferred (user instruction: don't run e2e myself).

### T-012: Relative path resolution for nudge prompts

### T-016: Project-local config overlay
Added two new global config keys: `currentWorkingDirectory.configFilePath` (default: `./.opencode/com.kevincojean.opencode-supernudge/supernudge-configuration.jsonc`) and `currentWorkingDirectory.configEnabled` (default: `true`). When enabled, plugin loads local config from resolved path (relative to `input.directory`). Local config overlays global: flat keys override, `prompts` array concatenates. Global-only keys (`configFilePath`, `configEnabled`) are preserved from global. Parse errors show toast (variant: "error") and fall back to global config. New functions: `loadLocalConfig`, `mergeConfigs`, `getMergedNudge` (replaces `getNudge`). 8 unit tests added, 2 e2e tests (AC15, AC16) added.
Prompt paths in config only supported `~` and `$HOME` expansion. Relative paths like `./prompts/tdd.md` or `prompts/tdd.md` would silently fail (`fs.existsSync` returns false -> prompt skipped). Fix: `resolvePath()` now takes a `baseDir` parameter (sourced from `PluginInput.directory` - opencode's working directory). After `~` and `$HOME` expansion, if the path is not absolute (`path.isAbsolute` returns false), it's resolved via `path.resolve(baseDir, p)`. This handles `./prompts/...`, bare `prompts/...`, and `../prompts/...` uniformly. `baseDir` is captured at plugin init time from `input.directory` and threaded through `getNudge(configPath, baseDir)` -> `resolvePrompts(prompts, defaults, baseDir)` -> `resolvePath(p, baseDir)`. Existing absolute and `~` paths unaffected (the `path.isAbsolute` check returns true for them, so they pass through unchanged). 3 unit tests added: `./` prefix, bare relative, `../` parent traversal. E2E AC12 added: creates prompt file at `projectDir/prompts/nudge.txt`, uses `./prompts/nudge.txt` in config, verifies nudge injected, cleans up after. 53/53 unit tests pass.

### T-017: Regex-based injection skip
Added `injection.skipOnRegexMatch: string[]` config key (default `[]`). When any regex pattern matches the text content at an injection point, that prompt's injection is skipped. Applies to all 4 injection paths: `chat.message`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`, `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.session.compacting`. Per-prompt overridable. Invalid regex patterns trigger a toast error (variant: "error") and are silently skipped. Match happens AFTER other plugins inject (checks the already-modified text). 6 unit tests added covering: chat.message skip, system.transform skip, messages.transform skip, compaction skip, per-prompt override, invalid regex handling. 2 e2e tests added (AC14, AC15). `ResolvedAutonomousPrompt` type updated to include the new field.

## 2026-10-25

### T-019: The `chat.message` limitation for invisible nudges
A `synthetic: true` part pushed from `chat.message` IS persisted but is STRIPPED from the prompt - the model never sees it. So `chat.message` can never deliver "model sees it, user does not". Only `experimental.chat.messages.transform` can. Verified against real opencode 1.18.27 with a stub LLM probe (`.omo/evidence/task-0-probe.txt`).

### T-019: Transform parts are memory-only
Parts inserted in `messages.transform` are never written to the `part` table and never returned by `session.messages()`. Consequence: no accumulation across turns, no stale-part cleanup, no dedupe logic needed. Each request gets exactly one fresh insertion.

### T-019: Hook ordering guarantee
`chat.message` runs before `messages.transform` in the same turn. Counters incremented in `chat.message` are safe to read from transform for that turn.

### T-019: Counter ownership under `nudge.visible`
The normalMessage counter is incremented ONLY in `chat.message`, and it increments even when `nudge.visible === false` (where delivery is skipped). The transform-side provider reads the counter and never increments. This keeps interval math identical across visibility modes.

### T-019: `computeDue` extraction
A single pure function drives both delivery paths so `injection.interval`, `injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage`, `injection.skipFirstMessageBelowChars` and `injection.skipOnRegexMatch` cannot diverge between visible and invisible mode.

### T-019: `nudge.visibleMarker` semantics
Means "suppress the wrapper", not "suppress the nudge". It wins over non-empty `wrapper.prefix`/`wrapper.suffix`. An empty wrapper string is a different feature and both must keep working.

### T-019: Block-level wrapper application
Both `chat.message` and the transform provider apply the wrapper ONCE per position group (start, end), not per prompt. Per-prompt wrapping broke multi-nudge tests which assert a single `<opencode-supernudge>` pair around several nudges.

### T-019: Synthetic part id convention
`prt_sn_${sessionID}_${partKey}`, deterministic. No id format is validated by the SDK; `prt_` is an internal convention only. `TextPart.synthetic` IS declared in `@opencode-ai/sdk`.

### T-019: Invisible handler placement inside the injector hook
The normalMessage invisible delivery lives INSIDE `SubAgentMessageInjector`'s single `experimental.chat.messages.transform` handler, reached via `setPrimaryInvisibleProvider`. A second hook key would be clobbered by the double `hooks()` spread in the plugin entry.

## 2026-08-25

### Orphaned opencode serve processes blocking e2e tests
e2e tests spawn opencode inside bwrap with `detached: true`. The `after` hook uses `process.kill(-proc.pid, "SIGKILL")` to kill the process group. But if the test runner crashes or is interrupted, the opencode process stays alive on the port. Next run: `spawnBwrap` fails with `Server exited code 1` because the port is already in use. Fix: kill orphaned `opencode serve` processes before running e2e tests: `pkill -9 -f "opencode serve"`.

### LLM proxy stub server replaces external dependency
e2e tests were hanging/timing out because they relied on a real LLM proxy at `localhost:8000`. Replaced with a lightweight Node `http.createServer` stub that returns canned OpenAI-compatible responses for `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`. Stub runs on `127.0.0.1:31000` on the host. bwrap with `--dev-bind / /` has network access, so opencode inside the sandbox can reach the stub. Tests went from 2+ minutes (or hanging) to ~57s. No external dependencies needed.

### alwaysOnFirstMessage was a no-op (pre-existing bug)
The shouldInject logic used OR: `(count === 1 && alwaysOnFirst) || interval <= 1 || (count - 1) % interval === 0`. The modulo condition `(count-1) % interval === 0` is always true for count=1 (0 % anything = 0), making `alwaysOnFirstMessage=false` ineffective. Fixed by restructuring: `interval <= 1 || (count === 1 ? alwaysOnFirst : (count - 1) % interval === 0)`.

### bwrap detached process unkillable - switched to direct spawn
E2E tests spawned `opencode serve` inside `bwrap` with `detached: true`. The `process.kill(-pid, "SIGKILL")` (process group kill) could not reach the opencode process inside the bwrap PID namespace. Tests would hang indefinitely because the server never died. Fix: `SN_E2E_NO_BWRAP=1` env var (now default in package.json) spawns `opencode serve` directly (no bwrap) with `detached: false`, `HOME` env var set to temp dir. Direct child process is killable with `proc.kill("SIGKILL")`. Added `process.exit(0)` in `after` hook with 1s delay to force exit even if child processes (LSP servers) keep pipes open. Added `--test-timeout=60000` to prevent infinite hangs.

### AC1 timeout at 30s - increased to 60s
AC1 sends 3 sequential prompts in one session via `sendMessages`. Each `client.session.prompt` is a full round-trip through opencode serve + stub LLM. 30s timeout was too tight for 3 round trips. Increased `--test-timeout` to 60000ms.

### AC10 deleted: contradicted T-001 bug fix part 2
AC10 expected autonomous nudge on PRIMARY agent messages, but T-001 bug fix part 2 explicitly blocks autonomous injection on primary sessions via `primarySessions` set. Test could never pass against current code. Deleted. Unit tests for subagent autonomous path (where `primarySessions` does NOT contain the session) remain valid and pass.

T-012 added AC12: creates `projectDir/prompts/nudge.txt`, config uses `./prompts/nudge.txt`, verifies nudge injected via `chat.message`. PASSES. Confirms `PluginInput.directory` is correctly threaded as `baseDir` through the real opencode runtime. Cleanup removes the created file and directory after assertion.

## 2026-09-04

### killOrphanedOpencode() killed user's running opencode serve process
The `killOrphanedOpencode()` function used `pkill -9 -f "opencode serve"` which matches ANY process with "opencode serve" in its command line - including the user's long-running `opencode serve` process. This caused the user's systemd-managed serve to die, requiring manual restart.

**Root cause**: `pkill -f` matches by full command line, not by PID or process group. The blanket kill was added in 2026-08-25 to clean up orphaned processes from crashed test runs, but it was too aggressive.

**Fix**: Removed `killOrphanedOpencode()` entirely. The scoped `killServer()` (kills by captured `proc.pid` + process group) already handles the test-spawned server correctly. For port conflicts, switched stub server to use port 0 (OS-assigned free port) and test server to use random high ports (40000-50000 range) to avoid conflicts with user's processes and orphaned test processes.

**Key insight**: Never use `pkill -f` with broad patterns in test cleanup - it will kill unintended processes. Prefer scoped cleanup by PID/process group, or use OS-assigned ports to avoid conflicts entirely.

### AC1 timing out at 60s - the real cause was a throwaway HOME, not ports
After removing `killOrphanedOpencode()` the suite kept timing out on AC1.
Two rounds of port fixes (scoped `fuser -k`, then random/OS-assigned ports) did not help.
Ports were never the problem.

**Evidence**: leftover `/tmp/sn-e2e-*` dirs from failed runs each contained a fully populated
`.config/opencode/node_modules` weighing **62MB**, plus a generated `package.json`
(`{"dependencies": {"@opencode-ai/plugin": "1.18.27"}}`) and a `package-lock.json`.
The `.cache/opencode/node_modules` dir was empty - opencode installs plugin deps into the
**config** dir, not the cache dir.

**Root cause**: `before` created a brand new `fs.mkdtempSync` HOME every run.
opencode then had to install 62MB of plugin dependencies from scratch on first boot.
npm's own cache lives at `$HOME/.npm`, which was also cold, so it was a full network download.
That cost landed on the first `session.prompt` call, i.e. inside AC1's 60s budget.
Network variance explains the flakiness: one run burned ~7 minutes and timed out
AC1/AC2/AC5/AC6/AC7/AC8/AC9 before warming up, later runs only blew AC1.

**Fix**:
1. Stable HOME at `/tmp/sn-e2e-home`, reused across runs (`resetE2eHome()`).
   It wipes only what a test can dirty - `opencode.jsonc`, `opencode-supernudge/`,
   `.local/share/opencode`, `.local/state/opencode`, `prompts/`, `nudge.txt`, `nonexistent.txt` -
   and preserves `node_modules`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`.
2. Warm-up `sendMessage("warm-up")` at the end of `before`, so plugin load and provider
   init are paid outside any test's budget. Counters are keyed by `sessionID`, and every
   test opens its own session, so the warm-up session cannot pollute assertions.
3. `before` hook given `{ timeout: 300000 }` so a genuinely cold first-ever run can finish.
4. AC1 given `{ timeout: 120000 }` - it is the only test doing 3 sequential round trips.
5. `spawnServer` boot timeout raised 15s -> 30s for cold-install runs.

**Key insight**: an isolated HOME is not free. Anything opencode installs per-HOME
(plugin deps, npm cache, provider packages) gets re-downloaded on every run and the bill
arrives inside the first test. Isolate config and session state, share the install.

### THE actual cause: non-streaming stub made opencode's agent loop spin forever
Stable HOME did not fix the timeouts, but it preserved `$HOME/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`
across runs - which finally showed the real failure.

**Evidence**: 422 consecutive `message=loop session.id=... step=N` lines, N counting 1 -> 421,
each preceded by a fresh `message=process messageID=<new>` and `message=stream`.
One user prompt, ~0.8s per step, running until the suite was killed.
Zero `level=ERROR` and zero `level=WARN` lines - the failure is completely silent.

**Root cause**: opencode calls the model through ai-sdk `streamText`, so the request body
carries `stream: true` and the provider expects `text/event-stream`.
The stub answered every request with a plain `application/json` chat-completion object.
The SSE parser found no events, so the assistant turn produced no text, no tool calls and
no finish reason. opencode saw an unfinished turn and stepped the loop again. Forever.
`client.session.prompt` only resolves when the loop ends, so the first prompt never returned.

**Why the suite looked like it "mostly passed" before**: every AC asserts on **user**
messages only. The nudge is written by `chat.message` before any LLM call. So whenever
`session.prompt` returned early for any reason, the assertion still passed - the assistant
never had to say anything. Only the tests that genuinely waited (AC1 first, then whichever
ran while the loop was hogging the server) surfaced as timeouts. This masked the bug for a
long time and sent three rounds of debugging at ports and npm installs instead.

**Fix**: the stub now parses the request body and branches on `stream === true`.
Streaming requests get real SSE - a content delta chunk, a `finish_reason: "stop"` chunk
with usage, then `data: [DONE]`. Non-streaming requests keep the old JSON shape.

**Key insight**: a stub for a streaming API must actually stream. If it does not, the
client does not error - it silently never finishes, and the symptom shows up as a test
timeout somewhere unrelated. Check the server log for a runaway `step=` counter before
blaming the test harness.

# Periodic nudge injection during autonomous agent/sub-agent work

Inject nudges periodically (every N turns) only while an agent or sub-agent is working autonomously. This is a SEPARATE counter from the existing user-message counter - they must not interfere.

Two distinct subagent-context toggles:

- `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge` (default `true`): injects the nudge into the subagent's initial system prompt via `experimental.chat.system.transform`. Existing behavior.
- `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge` (default `false`): master switch for the NEW periodic autonomous-nudge behavior. Drives `SubAgentMessageInjector`.

When `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=true` and `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge=false`, only the periodic path fires.
When `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=false` and `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge=true`, only the system-prompt path fires (legacy behavior).
When both `true`, both paths fire.

## Acceptance criteria (GivenWhenThen)

- Given `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=true` on a prompt, when N turns of autonomous agent/sub-agent work have elapsed since the last nudge for that prompt, then the configured nudges are injected into the next autonomous turn.
- Given a user sends a message via `chat.message`, when the user-message counter is incremented, then the autonomous counter is NOT affected.
- Given an autonomous turn is recorded (via `chat.message` for primary, via `experimental.text.complete` for subagent), when the autonomous counter is incremented, then the user-message counter is NOT affected.
- Given two prompts both have `enabled.subagentAutonomousWorkNudge=true` with different intervals, when turns happen, then each prompt's counter is evaluated independently against its own interval.

## Out of scope
- Subagent-specific scoping (tracked separately as T-002).
- Skipping by message content substrings (tracked separately as T-011).
- Deprecation of `enabled.subagent` -> replaced by `enabled.subagentSystemPromptNudge` (no compat shim).

# Scope nudge frequency per nudge prompt

## Problem
Currently ALL injection settings are global - one interval, one position, one enabled flag per channel applies to every prompt.
User wants per-prompt override capability: each prompt can override any subset of global settings.

## Current config shape
```jsonc
{
  "prompts": ["~/tdd.md", "~/givenwhenthen.md"],
  "injection.interval": 1,
  "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": true,
  "injection.resetCounterOnCompaction": true,
  "position.normalMessage": "start",
  "position.subagent": "start",
  "position.compaction": "start",
  "enabled.normalMessage": true,
  "enabled.subagent": true,
  "enabled.compaction": true
}
```

## Proposed config shape
Global keys become DEFAULTS. Each prompt entry can override any subset.

```jsonc
{
  "prompts": [
    "~/tdd.md",
    { "path": "~/givenwhenthen.md", "injection.interval": 3 },
    {
      "path": "~/no-mocking.md",
      "injection.interval": 1,
      "position.normalMessage": "end",
      "enabled.compaction": false
    }
  ],
  // these are now defaults for prompts that don't override them
  "injection.interval": 1,
  "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": true,
  "injection.resetCounterOnCompaction": true,
  "position.normalMessage": "start",
  "position.subagent": "start",
  "position.compaction": "start",
  "enabled.normalMessage": true,
  "enabled.subagent": true,
  "enabled.compaction": true
}
```

String entries = shorthand for `{ "path": entry }` (all defaults apply).

## Overridable keys per prompt
Every global key except `prompts` itself:
- `injection.interval`
- `injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage`
- `injection.resetCounterOnCompaction`
- `position.normalMessage`
- `position.subagent`
- `position.compaction`
- `enabled.normalMessage`
- `enabled.subagent`
- `enabled.compaction`

## Acceptance Criteria (GivenWhenThen)

### AC1: Per-prompt interval basic
Given config with two prompts having interval=1 and interval=3, when 3 messages sent, then prompt A injected on all 3, prompt B injected on 1st and 3rd only.

### AC2: Backward compat - string entries
Given config with prompts as string[] and global interval=2, when 3 messages sent, then all prompts inject on 1st and 3rd (global interval applies to all).

### AC3: Mixed string and object entries
Given config with prompts: ["~/a.md", { "path": "~/b.md", "injection.interval": 1 }] and global interval=3, when 3 messages sent, then a.md injects on 1st and 3rd, b.md injects on all 3.

### AC4: Per-prompt alwaysOnFirstMessage override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "injection.interval": 5, "injection.alwaysOnFirstMessage": false } and global alwaysOnFirst=true, when 1st message sent, then a.md NOT injected.

### AC5: Per-prompt interval with compaction reset
Given config with two prompts having different intervals and resetCounterOnCompaction=true, when compaction fires then next message sent, then both prompts inject (counter reset for all).

### AC6: Per-prompt enabled.normalMessage override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "enabled.normalMessage": false } and global enabled.normalMessage=true, when chat.message fires, then a.md NOT injected in user message, other prompts still inject.

### AC7: Per-prompt position.normalMessage override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "position.normalMessage": "end" } and global position.normalMessage=start, when chat.message fires, then a.md appended at end, other prompts at start.

### AC8: Per-prompt enabled.subagent override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "enabled.subagent": false } and global enabled.subagent=true, when system.transform fires, then a.md NOT in system array, other prompts still injected.

### AC9: Per-prompt position.subagent override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "position.subagent": "end" } and global position.subagent=start, when system.transform fires, then a.md at end of system array, others at start.

### AC10: Per-prompt enabled.compaction override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "enabled.compaction": false } and global enabled.compaction=true, when session.compacting fires, then a.md NOT in context array, other prompts still injected.

### AC11: Per-prompt position.compaction override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "position.compaction": "end" } and global position.compaction=start, when session.compacting fires, then a.md at end of context array, others at start.

### AC12: Per-prompt resetCounterOnCompaction override
Given config with { "path": "~/a.md", "injection.resetCounterOnCompaction": false, "injection.interval": 3 } and global resetCounterOnCompaction=true, when 1st message injects then compaction fires then 2nd message sent, then a.md does NOT inject on 2nd message (its counter was NOT reset, still at count=2, next inject at count=3).

## Out of Scope
- T-001 (autonomous turn injection) - separate task
- T-002 (per-agent scoping) - separate task
- T-004 (nudge title injection) - separate task
- T-005 (frontmatter stripping) - separate task

# Toggle nudge visibility (nudge.visible + nudge.visibleMarker)

Added two config keys controlling how nudges are delivered and marked:

- `nudge.visible` (default `true`): when `false`, the user message is left untouched and the nudge is delivered as a hidden `synthetic` text part via `experimental.chat.messages.transform`. The model sees it, the chat UI does not, and it is never persisted.
- `nudge.visibleMarker` (default `true`): when `false`, the `wrapper.prefix`/`wrapper.suffix` block is suppressed even if those strings are non-empty. The nudge text is still injected.

Both keys are overridable per-prompt. Interval math, `computeDue`, and counter ownership stay identical across visibility modes; delivery for `nudge.visible === false` happens inside the injector's single transform handler via `setPrimaryInvisibleProvider`.
